title: Go: Dependency Injection Container
description: Build a dependency injection container in Go using reflection for provider registration, automatic resolution, and lifetime management.

steps.title: Container with type registration
steps.description: Create a `Container` struct that stores providers as `map[reflect.Type]ProviderFunc`. Implement `Register(provider interface{})` that uses reflection to extract the return type of the provider function. Register a provider for `*Logger` and a provider for `*Database`. Print the registered types.
hints: Use `reflect.TypeOf(provider)` to get the function type, then `.Out(0)` for the return type

verification.successMessage: Container correctly registers providers by their return type!
verification.failureMessage: Print the registered types using fmt.Printf after each registration.

steps.title: Resolve with reflection
steps.description: Implement `Resolve(target interface{}) error` that takes a pointer to a struct and automatically populates its fields using reflection. For each field with a `@inject` tag, look up the provider and call it. Handle nested injection where a provider depends on another service. Print the resolved struct fields.
hints: Iterate struct fields, find tagged fields with `field.Tag.Get("inject")`
Look up the provider for the field type from the container registry
For nested dependencies, call `Resolve` recursively on the provider's own fields

verification.successMessage: Container resolves and injects dependencies recursively using field tags!
verification.failureMessage: Print the resolved struct showing all injected field values.

steps.title: Singleton lifetime
steps.description: Implement singleton scope where the provider is called once and the same instance is reused for all resolutions. Add a `RegisterSingleton` method that stores the instance after first creation. Register a `*Config` as singleton, resolve it twice, and print the pointer addresses to confirm they are the same object.
hints: Store singleton instances in a `map[reflect.Type]interface{}` on the container
On first Resolve, call the provider and cache the result in the singleton map
Print addresses: `fmt.Printf("%p\n", config)` to show same pointer on second call

verification.successMessage: Singleton lifetime returns the exact same instance across multiple resolutions!
verification.failureMessage: Print the pointer addresses to prove both resolutions return the same instance.

steps.title: Transient lifetime and scoped container
steps.description: Add transient lifetime (new instance every time) and scoped lifetime (one instance per scope). Implement `CreateScope()` that returns a new `Container` sharing singleton providers from the parent but with its own scope cache. Print memory addresses to demonstrate each lifetime behavior.
hints: Transient is the default — just call the provider every time without caching
Scoped container holds a reference to parent and its own instance cache
Resolve a service in two different scopes and print addresses to show different instances between scopes

verification.successMessage: Transient and scoped lifetimes correctly manage instance creation!
verification.failureMessage: Print pointer addresses showing transient gives new instances, scoped shares within scope.

steps.title: Circular dependency detection
steps.description: Implement circular dependency detection using a resolution stack. Before resolving a type, check if it is already in the resolution stack. If found, return a descriptive error. Test by creating two services that depend on each other and print the circular dependency error.
hints: Maintain a `map[reflect.Type]bool` or a slice as the resolution stack on the container
Push the type before resolving dependencies, pop after done — use defer for safety
On detecting a cycle, return an error: `fmt.Errorf("circular dependency: %s", t)`

verification.successMessage: Circular dependency detection catches and reports dependency cycles with clear errors!
verification.failureMessage: Print the circular dependency error message when a cycle is detected.
